newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - Gasoline stocks to near surplus in APIs.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Gasoline stocks to near surplus in APIs.

text.p: American Petroleum Institute's (API) weekly oil inventory data Wednesday evening is expected to show a build in gasoline stocks, the first in a series that could lead to a year-over-year stock surplus by March, analysts said.

"There is a possibility for a surplus by that time (March). The refiners have had incentive to make gasoline for about a month," said Linda Abramo, analyst with Energy Security Analysis Inc. Trader estimates of stock data ranged from steady to a two million barrel rise in gasoline stocks.

Higher output of gasoline for the week ended February 14 is anticipated to result in a build despite an increase in demand which fell to a two-year low of about 6.70 million barrels a day the week before.
The prompt gasoline-to-crude spread, a part of refiner profitability, has risen from $3.00 a barrel in mid-January to about $4.50 this week.

Gasoline imports are expected to ease somewhat, but the refinery utilization rate is seen rising up to one percentage point as many refineries emerge from a particularly busy winter maintenance schedule.
"All the refiners should be back by April and plenty of gasoline should be available," said John Lichtblau, president of Petroleum Industry Research Foundation in New York.
By the end March of last year, the year-over-year gasoline deficit was about 10 million barrels. As of February 7, 1997 gasoline stocks was a mere 3.4 million barrels below a year ago.
Meanwhile, crude stocks are seen rising by up to four million barrels, helped in part by steady imports with refinery run rates still relatively low at below 90 percent.
Distillate stocks were seen falling up to three million barrels, reflecting a seasonal tendency for those stocks to decline as refiners switch their output focus to gasoline.
Refiners are said to be building gasoline stocks ahead of summer when demand typically peaks.
